newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives FrontierVision 2006 notes B rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives FrontierVision 2006 notes B rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it assigned a B rating to FrontierVision Operating Partners L.P.'s $200 million senior subordinated notes, due 2006.
The corporate credit rating was BB minus, S&P said.
The outlook on the ratings was stable, it said in a statement.

"FrontierVision Operating Partners' issuer credit rating reflects the stable cash flow generating ability of its cable TV systems, tempered by the partnership's small size and fairly high debt relative to expected cash flow," S&P said.
The recently formed partnership owns and has agreed to acquire cable TV operations in nonurban regions of Maine, Vermont, Ohio, Kentucky, and other states in the southeast.

The systems, with an expected total 353,800 basic subscribers, have high basic penetration of 71 percent pro forma, and exhibit the strong and stable operating statistics and cash generation of cable operations required for reception.
Issue proceeds, along with partnership contributions, will finance $244 million in pending cable system acquisitions in the above states, S&P said.
"These purchases will give FrontierVision ample opportunities to consolidate technical and customer service functions improving both system profitability and service quality," S&P said.

Cash flow interest coverage starts out at a fairly good 1.4 times, relative to its peer-group, and debt to cash flow in line with the rating at 6.7 times, S&P said. Modest improvement in key credit indicators is expected, it added
"The rating factors in expectations of cash flow growth due to cost reduction and improved efficiency," S&P said.
Additional acquisitions of similar cable systems are likely, which will limit the partnership's ability to lower its debt relative to cash flow generation for the next several years, S&P.
